parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the trend in the reactivity of the halogens $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ as oxidising agents. Explain this trend using values of $E^{\ominus}$ ($\text{X}_2/\text{X}^-$) from the Data Booklet.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between chlorine and water.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use standard electrode potential, $E^{\ominus}$, data from the Data Booklet to calculate the $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$ for the following reaction.

$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The $[\text{OH}^-]$ was increased and the $E_{\text{cell}}$ was measured.

Indicate how the value of the $E_{\text{cell}}$ measured would compare to the $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$ calculated in (ii) by placing one tick (✓) in the table.

| $E_{\text{cell}}$ becomes less positive than $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$. |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| $E_{\text{cell}}$ stays the same as $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$. |  |
| $E_{\text{cell}}$ becomes more positive than $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$. |  |

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
A half-equation involving bromate(V) ions, $\text{BrO}_3^-$, and bromide ions is shown.

$$\text{BrO}_3^-(\text{aq}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) + 6\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Br}^-(\text{aq}) + 6\text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \quad E^{\ominus} = +0.58\text{ V}$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
An alkaline solution of chlorate(I), $\text{ClO}^-$, can be used to oxidise bromide ions to bromate(V) ions.

Use the Data Booklet and the half-equation shown to write an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$ for the reaction in (i).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
When a concentrated solution of bromic(V) acid, $\text{HBrO}_3$, is warmed, it decomposes to form bromine, oxygen and water only.

Write an equation for this reaction. The use of oxidation numbers may be helpful.
